seasonSpecificColumns.defensive_contribution: 2025-26 onward, when defensive-contribution scoring was introduced

excludedRows.rule: Rows whose position column is not GK/GKP, DEF, MID or FWD are not footballers and are dropped.
excludedRows.reason: The only season that ever had them is 2024-25 (assistant managers, position "AM"). They record no minutes and no starts, so every feature describing them is zero, and their points came entirely from mng_* columns that no other season has. Keeping them would put an abolished scoring system into both the training set and the held-out block.

seasonWeighting.formula: weight = 0.5 ** (seasonsOld / halfLifeSeasons), seasonsOld counted back from the newest season
seasonWeighting.note: null means off, every row weighted 1. Selected per target by validation metric; ties go to off.

baseline: Season points per game carried forward: predict this gameweek with the mean points the player has scored per played gameweek so far this season.

points.selectionRationale: Validation RMSE. The optimizer sums expected points over a squad, so it needs an unbiased conditional mean; MAE targets the conditional median, which understates a zero-inflated, right-skewed target. MAE is reported for every candidate alongside it.

engineConsumesDisabledBecause: This artifact loads at runtime and nothing in it reaches the engine. Its start calibrator does beat its own statistical baseline on held-out data (test log loss 0.3006 against a 0.3135 baseline, expected calibration error 0.0447 improved to 0.0221), and it still costs season points. Two leakage-free full-season replays were run. In each one a model was trained EXCLUDING the season about to be replayed, then that season was replayed with and without it. 2024-25, model trained on 2022-23 and 2023-24 only: planner 2371 to 2211 (-160), greedy-xp 2284 to 2215 (-69), hold 2006 to 1953 (-53), and projection bias moved from +0.33 points per gameweek to +2.6 points per gameweek. 2023-24, model trained on 2022-23, 2024-25 and 2025-26: planner 1943 to 1853 (-90), greedy-xp 1947 to 1892 (-55), hold 1928 to 1944 (+16). Both seasons and both decision-making strategies moved the same way, and the planner's edge over the greedy baseline collapsed from +87 to -4 in 2024-25. Conclusion: the artifact beats its statistical baseline but degrades season points in leakage-free replay, so nothing from it is fed to the engine. startCalibratorJSON is kept in this file on purpose so the decision can be re-tested later, with scripts/backtest.mjs --model against a season the artifact was not trained on. A better log loss on its own is not grounds to re-enable this.
pointsModelNotConsumedBecause: beatsBaselineOnTest compares the points model against points per game carried forward. The engine projects points by convolving component distributions, not by carrying a mean forward, so clearing the naive baseline is not evidence it would improve the engine. That is a separate measurement against projections.js, and it has not been run.
